rules.rule: Check for collapse following vaccination features
rules.problem: Type and trigger are right, and every red-box/discriminating feature of the Delayed column is listed, but the page's primary discriminators between the two columns are timing (sudden vs delayed) and duration of loss of consciousness (20 s-1 min relieved by lying down vs > 1 min not relieved), and none is checked for. SNOMED has Sudden onset / Delayed onset (qualifier value) and Brief loss of consciousness / Prolonged loss of consciousness (finding), all confirmed with exists. 'Pulse may be slow' (Pulse slow, finding) is also unchecked, though it is optional on the page.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable fainting episode following vaccination
rules.problem: 'Fainting episode likely' -> probable Syncope and the 'no other signs' negations are faithful, but (a) no Sudden onset qualifier on Collapse, so a delayed collapse with normal vitals is called a faint; (b) SBP >= 90 and DBP >= 60 are required although the page says BP is 'briefly low but rapidly normal again', so a reading taken during the dip blocks the diagnosis; (c) the LOC-duration criterion is absent. Only the no-features list actually comes from the Sudden column.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable anaphylaxis after collapse following vaccination
rules.problem: The flat 'or' makes any single feature sufficient: collapse + vaccination + one cough, one rash, or one BP reading < 90/60 (which the page says also happens briefly in a faint) yields probable anaphylaxis, with no requirement that the collapse was delayed, that LOC lasted > 1 min, or that BP 'remains low'. The page describes a cluster for the Delayed column. Suggested shape: (and Collapse+Delayed onset, Vaccination given, (or (any2 of the vital/airway/skin features) Prolonged loss of consciousness)). Probable level is defensible for 'Treat as anaphylaxis'; no priority evaluation is needed here because page 20's 'Urgent: Anaphylaxis' fires on the active condition.

summary: The anaphylaxis rule over-fires: any one feature (a single BP < 90/60 reading, a cough, a rash) after any collapse post-vaccination gives probable anaphylaxis, while the page's Delayed-collapse column is a cluster keyed on delayed timing, LOC > 1 minute and BP that remains low. The fainting rule conversely requires BP >= 90/60 although the page says BP is briefly low in a faint, and neither rule carries the sudden/delayed onset or LOC-duration discriminators that the page actually uses (Sudden onset, Delayed onset, Brief/Prolonged loss of consciousness all exist in SNOMED and are not checked for). Concept choices (Collapse, Vaccination given, Syncope, Anaphylaxis, the airway and skin findings, Pulse, function) are all correct and verbatim-supported.
